result.title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
result.summary: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent's investigation and assessment. Our work contributes a collaborative workflow and agent design that use author knowledge to guide reproducibility auditing. The conference deployment provides empirical evidence that this approach can help identify and address reproducibility problems through collaboration among authors, agents, and reviewers.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「作者参与式」协作可复现性审计流程：用结构化清单记录复现说明，在 GitHub 两阶段工作流中让 agent 检查、作者澄清修订后再评估，并在 36 篇会议论文、133 个图表上部署验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把外部声明作为 agent 调查的显式输入、并分开判定「是否已复现」与「是否需澄清/修复」的做法，可能为 LVR 中证据获取与停止/升级决策的评价设计提供参照，但领域相距较远，可供核查。
